negative_findings: Real wages (Orkla-weighted, Nordic, NO, SE) and real disposable income show no robust positive (demand) effect on the implied volume proxy at any horizon. The full-sample t-stats of 0.6-1.9 turn negative without 2021Q3-23Q4.
Real-wage associations with margins and organic growth come from their CPI component. The SE real-wage-acceleration effect on d_margin drops to t of about 0 once SE CPI acceleration is controlled.
Consumer confidence (levels or changes; Orkla-weighted, Nordic, Finans Norge, EC Sweden) has no BY-significant relation with d_margin at any alignment, and no robust positive relation with volume.
Consumer confidence relates negatively to og, the opposite of a 'confidence drives sales' story.
Policy-rate levels and bond-yield levels are uninformative for d_margin (|t|<1.5 at every alignment).
Yield levels relate only weakly to the volume proxy: t about -2.8 at h=1, BY q=0.45.

For quarterly d_margin, no core feature is BY-significant at h=2 or h=4 in the full sample. Predictability beyond 1 quarter comes only from the delayed pass-through in the lag scan, and from the sample without 2021Q3-23Q4 at h=4.
The volume proxy is unpredictable in real time: 0 core features pass BY at h=1, h=2 or h=4. The lag scan finds only the mechanical food-CPI term at k=0.
og predictability is largely the 2021Q3-2023Q4 episode: within the ex-inflation families only 0-3 of 200 core features pass BY at each alignment, although signs persist with t of about 2-3.7.
FX (Orkla-weighted, NOK and SEK crosses): no FX feature passes BY for d_margin, og or volume. The only BY hits are for d_og at h=4, a base effect via imported inflation.
Energy (Nordic electricity, EU gas, Brent in NOK) is never BY-significant for d_margin or og. EU gas and electricity do lead d_og at h=1-4.
Nominal wage growth (w_wage_yoy/dyoy, SE wage index, NO food-manufacturing earnings) is insignificant for margins (|t|<2).
Unemployment change predicts same-quarter margin gains (t=+4.2), but this falls to t=+1.7 (+0.5 at h=0) once packaging-cost inflation is controlled.
Many all-family hits are likely spurious or very-small-weight series: RO, LV and LT bond yields, the CZ policy rate, NO border-trade series (2009+), and short EU cereal series (n<40).
key_numbers: Discovery tests: 5,964 core (200 features x 6 targets x 5 alignments, minus n<30); 42,180 all-feature; 8,316 lag scan (200 x 7 lags x 6 targets). BY is applied within each target x alignment family of about 200 or about 1,400 tests.
Global BY across all 5,964 core tests: 844 survive at q<0.10. Across the 2,982 primary-target tests: 406 survive.
BY-significant / robust core features by alignment (coin, h=0, h=1, h=2, h=4):
Episode dependence: packaging PPI vs d_margin has t=-9.6 in the full sample but -3.1 without 2021Q3-23Q4. SE food CPI vs og: +11.5 full, +3.5 without the episode.
Delayed margin pass-through: cost/price inflation 6-7 quarters back has t=+4.2 to +5.2 vs d_margin, with own lag +3.4 to +4.5 and without 2021Q3-23Q4 +4.3 to +5.6.
Base effect: corr(d_og_t, og_{t-4}) = -0.64, against -0.37 for d_og's own lag 4.
Implied volume proxy vs reported volume/mix (2022Q2-26Q2, n=17): r=0.83, MAE 1.85pp, bias -0.35pp. Weighted food CPI ex VAT vs reported price: r=0.92 (Nordic version 0.95).
The numpy HAC estimator matches common.nw_ols to 1.2e-13 in t-stats.
Effect sizes per 1 sd of the feature: input-cost features move d_margin by about 0.5-0.6pp; food CPI moves og by about 1.7pp; the best d_og predictors move it by 1.3-2.1pp.
caveats: The 2022-23 inflation episode is the only large, well-measured cost shock. It forms a high-leverage cluster that inflates HAC t-stats; the leverage-adjusted HAC t and the sample without 2021Q3-23Q4 are the honest tests and are reported for every feature.
Even with HAC, small-sample t-stats on about 100 autocorrelated quarters are optimistic. The rolling-4Q targets (d_margin_r4, d_og_r4) overlap heavily, so their t-stats are descriptive only.

A univariate screen cannot separate proxies from causes. Real wages and confidence mostly proxy inflation, and yield changes proxy the cost/inflation cycle, though they survive cost controls. Only targeted two-variable conditional checks were run.
Many d_og predictors work through the base effect. The +base column (control for og_{t-L}) should be checked before treating a d_og predictor as new information.
Macro data are latest vintage: publication lags are respected, revisions are not.
The Orkla-weighted composites use geographic weights from annual reports published after year end (mild look-ahead), and confidence z-scores use full-sample scaling.

Definition mix is only partly handled by dummies and quality weights: India inside the headline 2014Q4-2022Q2; Rieber, Hame and Eastern acquisitions inside d_margin; distribution agreements counted as organic in 2015-16; low-precision og in 2001-05.
Easter controls (easter_shift) are proxies, and the sign of the Easter effect is ambiguous.
The volume proxy fails in 2025, when consumer food CPI (about 4%) ran ahead of Orkla's own pricing (about 1%). Features correlated with food CPI also correlate mechanically negatively with the proxy.

Features are highly redundant (FAO/WB indices in several currencies, packaging sub-indices), so the number of independent signals is far smaller than the test count. The figures de-duplicate at |corr|>0.9.

common.py note 1: d_og_r4 compares headline og_est with og_est shifted 4 quarters, so it crosses definitions in 2008Q1-09Q1, 2013Q1-15Q4 and 2022Q3-24Q1. That includes the D->E break that d_og itself avoids, and no flag is provided. Worked around locally with a constructed d_og_r4_break control; common.py was not modified.
common.py note 2: nw_ols drops NaN and zero-weight rows, so quarters on either side of a gap are treated as adjacent in the Newey-West lags. The effect is minor and was replicated for consistency.

Deliverables: screen_results_core.csv, screen_results_all.csv, lag_profiles.csv, lag_best.csv, and 18 PNGs in figures/ (top10_<target>_{coincident,realtime}.png and lagprofile_<target>.png for 6 targets).
Scripts (reproducible, about 4 minutes): screen_lib.py, run_screen.py, make_figures.py, write_findings.py.
